Anti-HIV agents must be avoided from at least one month before stem cell mobilisation until at least 7 days after infusion of Zynteglo.

Based on data with the potent enzyme inducer rifampicin, a substantial reduction (perhaps up to an 80 % decrease) in the concentration of zopiclone is expected. Minimal changes are expected in the concentration of carbamazepine and the active metabolite carbamazepine epoxide. If the patient is already taking zopiclone and starts carbamazepine, there will be an increased risk of central nervous system adverse effects/adverse cognitive effects during the first few days, before the induction effect occurs.

Treatment with iron chelators must be interrupted 7 days before starting myeloablative conditioning. When using iron chelators during the first six months after infusion of Zynteglo, non-myelosuppressive chelators should be chosen over chelators that may cause myelosuppression.

Substantially decreased concentration of erythromycin. It is uncertain whether the concentration of phenytoin is affected. Although there are studies showing no effect on the phenytoin concentration, an increased concentration of phenytoin in individual patients cannot be ruled out.

Substantially increased risk of bleeding, including an increased risk of fatal cerebral haemorrhage. In a study with streptokinase, the risk of death increased from 19 % without concomitant use of acetylsalicylic acid to 34 % with concomitant use of acetylsalicylic acid, mainly due to cerebral haemorrhages. Similar findings have been shown in a more recent study with alteplase, where the risk of intracerebral haemorrhage increased from 1,6 % to 4,3 %.

An increase in the concentration of tetrahydrocannabinol (80 %) and cannabidiol (twofold) has been shown for the potent enzyme inhibitor ketoconazole. However, fluconazole is a weaker inhibitor than ketoconazole of CYP3A4, which is mainly responsible for the metabolism of cannabidiol, but a stronger inhibitor than ketoconazole of CYP2C9, which is responsible for the metabolism of tetrahydrocannabinol. The increase in concentration may therefore be expected to be greater than stated above for tetrahydrocannabinol, but smaller than stated above for cannabidiol.

An increased concentration of chloramphenicol has been demonstrated in one study, and a decreased concentration in another study. However, both studies have been heavily criticised on methodological grounds, and the findings are highly uncertain. Other studies show no interaction.

In a study in healthy volunteers, an increased concentration of midostaurin (approximately 10 times) and active metabolites (3-4 times) was found with concomitant use of the potent CYP3A4 inhibitor ketoconazole. A substantially smaller effect has been shown in patients with itraconazole, an enzyme inhibitor that is in principle equally potent. These conflicting results are surprising and cannot be explained by the results presented in the summary of product characteristics for midostaurin. In addition, a clinical study in approximately 200 patients showed that the concentration of midostaurin increased by only 40-50 % during concomitant treatment with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors.

A substantially smaller effect has been shown in patients with itraconazole, an enzyme inhibitor that is in principle equally potent. These conflicting results are surprising and cannot be explained by the results presented in the summary of product characteristics for midostaurin. The summary of product characteristics for pirfenidone recommends that smoking should be avoided during treatment with pirfenidone and that patients should be encouraged to stop smoking. The active clopidogrel metabolite is reduced by up to 40-50 % for omeprazole and esomeprazole and somewhat less for lansoprazole and pantoprazole. The higher the dose of the proton pump inhibitor, the greater the effect. This leads to a reduced antiplatelet effect measured in blood samples from healthy volunteers and patients.
